issue_context.title: Speedtest runs at boot/restart with polling update disabled
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Since the update/changes in 2023.01 (https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/84295) the speedtest behaviour is changed.
In a response to that I disabled polling update from system options, where I like to just trigger the speedtest myself. All fine so far, but after a restart it runs on it's own, which is unexpected and imho undesirable and unnecessary.

In my humble opinion it should not do a speedtest at startup when polling update is disabled where it unnecessary slows things down within HA and might negatively effect other activities happening on the internet connection during day-/work-time.



### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2023.2.3

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2022.12.x

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

SpeedTest

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/speedtestdotnet

### Diagnostics information

Not applicable. It's undesirable behavior.

_No response_

review_comments: This should not be handled here IMHO, we already handling polling preferences in the coordinator, to me it seems like this is a miss.

Here we are disabling the initial refresh at startup. To my understanding even if polling is disabled in system options the initial coordinator refresh is executed for each integration that uses the coordinator at startup. For this integration we were adding an option to skip the initial refresh if polling is disabled (leaving the user with automating when the refresh should happen).
